content.title: Language and Accessibility
How to read "must", "should" and "may" in this manual
items: MUST — mandatory. The school has no choice. The law requires it, or Cambridge requires it of the school as a centre, or Eduversal requires it as a condition of network membership. Not complying is a finding.

SHOULD — strongly recommended. This is the practice Eduversal expects. A school that departs from it should be able to explain why. A single departure is not a finding on its own, but a pattern of departures is.

MAY — permitted and optional. The school decides. Sometimes "may" is used to mean "might happen". In those places, the sentence is rewritten to say so. This is because "may" alone is unclear in English: it can mean permission or possibility.
This manual does not use "shall". Where older material used it, read it as "must".
If a statement has no rule word (modal) at all, it is descriptive. It explains how something works. It does not create a duty.
Sometimes a duty appears in two places with a different rule strength. Then the stronger reading applies until the conflict is resolved. Report the conflict to Eduversal so the text can be corrected.

content.text: Our Aspirational Future: To be a transformative network of Cambridge schools across Indonesia, recognized internationally for academic excellence, innovative pedagogy, and developing globally competent, ethically grounded learners who thrive in a rapidly changing world.
content.title: VISION

content.text: Our Purpose and Commitments: We exist to:
content.title: MISSION

steps: Deliver world-class, Cambridge-standard education that challenges and supports every student to achieve their highest potential academically, socially, and emotionally.
Cultivate exceptional educators through continuous professional development, collaborative practice, and access to cutting-edge pedagogical approaches.
Prepare students for global competitiveness by providing opportunities in international academic competitions (including olympiads), university pathways, and real-world problem-solving.
Build a network of educational excellence by sharing best practices, resources, and expertise across our partner schools and the wider Indonesian education community.
Integrate Indonesian values and identity into an international curriculum framework, ensuring students are rooted in the Pancasila principles while remaining globally aware.
Provide comprehensive educational consultancy that elevates teaching quality, curriculum design, and institutional effectiveness across our network and beyond.

content.text: The Principles That Guide Us
content.title: CORE VALUES

content.text: We set high standards and pursue continuous improvement in all aspects of our work. Every student and staff member can achieve excellence through effort, support, and reflective practice.
content.title: EXCELLENCE (Keunggulan)

content.text: We act with honesty, ethical responsibility, and transparency. Our decisions and actions align with our commitments to students, families, and the wider community.
content.title: INTEGRITY (Integritas)

content.text: We embrace change, take calculated risks, and continuously seek better ways to teach, learn, and lead. We leverage technology and research-informed practices to enhance learning outcomes.
content.title: INNOVATION (Inovasi)

content.text: We value diversity and ensure equitable access to high-quality education. We recognize and respond to the varied learning needs, backgrounds, and strengths of all students and staff.
content.title: INCLUSIVITY (Inklusivitas)

content.text: We believe in the power of teamwork, shared leadership, and learning communities. We collaborate within and across schools to achieve outcomes no single person or institution could accomplish alone.
content.title: COLLABORATION (Kolaborasi)

content.text:
We develop students who understand their Indonesian identity while engaging confidently and responsibly with diverse cultures, perspectives, and global challenges.

SOCIAL CONTRIBUTION (Pengabdian Sosial): We encourage students to contribute meaningfully to their communities, embodying empathy, responsibility, and global citizenship.
content.title: GLOBAL CITIZENSHIP (Kewarganegaraan Global)

content.text: The Capacities We Develop in Every Graduate By the time students complete their education within the Eduversal network, they will demonstrate:
content.title: SCHOOLWIDE LEARNER OUTCOMES (SLOs)

items: Master rigorous content across disciplines aligned to Cambridge standards
Apply analytical reasoning, inquiry, and evidence-based problem-solving
Demonstrate intellectual curiosity and self-directed learning habits
content.title: 1. Academic Excellence & Critical Thinking

items: Express ideas clearly and persuasively in English and Bahasa Indonesia, across written, oral, and digital formats
Listen actively and engage respectfully in dialogue with diverse audiences
Collaborate productively in teams and negotiate meaning across cultures
content.title: 2. Effective Communication

items: Understand Indonesian history, values (Pancasila), and cultural heritage
Engage knowledgeably with global issues, perspectives, and interdependencies
Navigate diverse cultural contexts with empathy, respect, and adaptability
content.title: 3. Global Competence & Cultural Awareness

items: Act with integrity, honesty, and respect for others
Take initiative to address challenges in their communities and beyond
Demonstrate environmental stewardship and commitment to sustainable practices
content.title: 4. Ethical Leadership & Social Responsibility

items: Apply creative thinking and design processes to solve complex problems
Use technology responsibly and effectively to enhance learning and productivity
Embrace change with resilience, flexibility, and a growth mindset
content.title: 5. Innovation & Adaptability

items: Practice self-regulation, reflection, and responsible decision-making
Maintain physical, mental, and emotional health through balanced living
Set and pursue meaningful goals with perseverance and self-discipline
content.title: 6. Personal Wellbeing & Self-Awareness

content.text: Eduversal Partner Schools work under a collaborative governance model. It balances:
content.title: Governance Philosophy

items: Network consistency through shared standards, systems and expertise
School autonomy (freedom) in operational decisions and in responding to its local context
Accountability to students, families, regulatory bodies, and educational standards

content.text: Yayasan Edukasi Universal Indonesia (Eduversal) Board of Trustees
content.title: Level 1: Eduversal Foundation (Network Level)

items: Composition: 5-7 members with expertise in education, finance, law, and governance
Chair: Ketua Umum Yayasan
Term: 3-year terms, renewable
Meeting Frequency: Quarterly (minimum); extra meetings as needed

content.text: Responsibilities:

items: Approve network-wide strategic direction and 5-year plans
Keep the network financially sustainable and oversee its finances as trustees (fiduciary oversight)
Appoint and evaluate the Chief Academic Officer and senior network leadership
Approve major capital spending, new school partnerships and policy frameworks
Monitor compliance with Indonesian regulations, Cambridge standards, and accreditation requirements
Protect the mission, vision and values of Eduversal

content.text: Executive Director

items: Reports to: Board of Trustees
Appointed and evaluated by: Board of Trustees
Be accountable, as the executive, for Eduversal as a whole — its strategic, operational and institutional direction
Oversee all divisions as the executive and keep them in line with Eduversal’s vision and values
Be the person the Chief Academic Officer reports to on operational matters
Represent Eduversal to the Board of Trustees on institutional and non-academic matters

content.text: Chief Academic Officer

items: Reports to: Executive Director (operational line); appointed and evaluated by the Board of Trustees (through the Chair)
Chairs the Eduversal Academic Board
Lead implementation of network strategy and academic standards
Oversee Quality Management System (QMS) across all schools
Manage staff rotation, appraisal, and professional development programs
Coordinate Cambridge compliance, accreditation, and examination integrity
Monitor school performance against KPIs and SLOs (Schoolwide Learner Outcomes)
Support General Managers with coaching and resources
Support collaboration and knowledge sharing across the network

content.text: Eduversal Academic Board

items: Chaired by: Chief Academic Officer
Composition: ten Subject Specialists at three seniority ranks — Director (3), Consultant (3), Coordinator (4)

The three Director-rank Specialists also each serve as director of a division: Primary Education, Secondary Education and Islamic Schools. Rank shows seniority, not a reporting line. Every member reports to the Chief Academic Officer.

Decision authority: the Board decides network academic standards, teacher and school appraisal instruments, EASE program assessment content, and seminar topics by agreement. For EASE tests, the Chief Academic Officer gives the final sign-off before publication
A seminar topic is not delivered in schools until the Board has agreed on it

The Board is also the school-visiting team. Five Specialists attend each School Appraisal visit, one for each domain. Each domain is owned by two Domain Leads, and the pair is split across a school’s two visits (see clause 24.2)
Members hold the confidential appraisal record. Internal visit documents are restricted to Board members

content.text: Local Yayasan Role:
content.title: Level 2: Partner School Foundation (School Ownership Level)

items: Legal owner of school facilities, land, and operational licenses
Holds NPSN and Ministry permits
Legal employer (employer of record) of all staff at the school
Financial sponsor of school operations, under the MOU (Memorandum of Understanding) with Eduversal

content.text: Responsibilities:

items: Provide funding for operational expenses, salaries, and capital improvements
Ensure compliance with regulations and local licensing
Coordinate with the General Manager (Eduversal representative) on budget and reporting
Approve the annual school budget in consultation with Eduversal and the GM
Take part in annual evaluation meetings with Eduversal leadership

content.text: Decision Rights:

items: Approve the school’s annual budget (after the GM drafts it)
Approve major capital projects and facility changes
Review and endorse significant policy changes proposed by Eduversal/GM
Resolve disputes escalated by the GM (in consultation with Eduversal)

content.text: Note: Day-to-day management authority is delegated to the General Manager under the 20-year partnership MOU.
Appointment: Assigned by Eduversal. Serves as Eduversal's on-site representative, with full management authority. Reports to:
content.title: Level 3: School Leadership (Operational Level)

items: Functionally: Chief Academic Officer
Administratively: Local Yayasan (for carrying out the budget and for compliance reporting)

content.text: Responsibilities:

items: Full operational authority over school management, curriculum, staffing, and student affairs
Develop an annual School Improvement Plan (SIP) in line with the network strategy
Draft and carry out the annual school budget, working with the local Yayasan
Run the QMS (Quality Management System) programs (DTP, Appraisal, EduOS, EduNav, EASE)

Recruit and supervise principals, teachers and staff, and evaluate teachers and staff through the school's appraisal processes. In each principal's appraisal, act as the governance-side co-reviewer and co-sign the summary. The primary appraiser is the Chief Academic Officer or a designated Academic Director.
Ensure safeguarding, child protection, and student well-being
Represent Eduversal in all dealings with local authorities, parents, and the community
Submit twice-yearly reports to Eduversal and local Yayasan
Check that all school-level data in Dapodik correctly shows the school’s licensing, facility status and NPSN registration
Ensure that the local Yayasan's funding and operational licenses match the data submitted to the Ministry of Education
School administration should monitor official tax payments and other related official financial transactions.

content.text: Decision Rights:

items: Hire/terminate non-rotational staff (in consultation with HR)
Approve curriculum adaptations within the Cambridge framework
Set the school calendar and daily operations
Manage student admissions and discipline (within policy)
Allocate budget within approved parameters
Emergency decisions (with post-hoc reporting)

content.text:
Appointment: Assigned by the Foundation Representative / General Manager, in consultation with Eduversal.

Role Structure: The Principal's role may be organized by educational level, depending on school size and structure:

steps: Early Years Principal: TK/KB (ages 3-6)
Primary School Principal: Grades 1-6 (Cambridge Primary)
Secondary School Principals:

items: Junior High School Principal: Grades 7-9 (Cambridge Lower Secondary, IGCSE)
Senior High School Principal: Grades 10-12 (IGCSE, AS/A Level)

content.text: In smaller schools, one Principal may oversee several levels. In larger schools, separate Principals report to the Foundation Representative / General Manager. They work together through the SLT (Senior Leadership Team). Core Competencies (in line with Permendikdasmen No. 21/2025, Standar Tenaga Kependidikan, which replaced Permendiknas No. 13/2007): All Principals must show competency in:

steps: Kepribadian (Personality): Integrity, work ethic, self-development
Managerial: Planning, organizing, leading, monitoring
Kewirausahaan (Entrepreneurship): Innovation, risk-taking, school improvement
Supervision: Teacher observation, instructional coaching, quality assurance
Sosial: Collaboration, communication, community relations

content.text:
Reports to: General Manager

Responsibilities:

steps: Academic and instructional leadership at assigned level(s)
Implement the Cambridge curriculum and Indonesian national subjects
Lead Professional Learning Communities (PLCs) and teacher appraisal
Supervise Subject Leaders and department heads
Oversee student support services (EAL, SEN, Counseling)
Manage day-to-day student discipline and parent communication
Collaborate with Eduversal Directors (Primary/Secondary Education)
Support school improvement planning and evaluation
Ensure compliance with Cambridge Centre requirements.
Oversee the accuracy of teacher data in Dapodik and SIMPKB. Ensure every educator is registered under the correct NUPTK for appraisal and certification.

Check that student enrollment, attendance rules and academic progression are recorded correctly in Dapodik. This keeps student records valid for national examinations and for the Profil Pelajar Pancasila (P5) documentation.
Work with the Pengawas Sekolah (School Supervisor) to ensure that school-level data matches Ministry inspection protocols and the Panduan Kerja Kepala Sekolah.
Ensure that national reporting systems correctly show how Indonesian mandatory subjects are integrated, while keeping Cambridge standards.

content.text: Decision Rights:

steps: Classroom observations and teacher coaching
Timetabling and class assignments within the assigned level
Student academic grouping and interventions
Co-curricular program design
Minor operational adjustments (within GM-approved policy)
Recommendation for teacher hiring/termination (final decision: GM)

content.text: Matrix Collaboration:

steps: Functional guidance: Eduversal Director of Primary/Secondary Education
Direct supervision: General Manager / Foundation Representative
Regulatory oversight: Pengawas Sekolah (School Supervisor)

content.text: Composition:

items: General Manager (Chair)
Principal
Vice Principal(s) / Wakil Kepala Sekolah (Academic, Student Affairs, Operations as applicable)
Heads of Department (HODs) for core subjects
EAL/SEN Coordinator
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)

content.text: Responsibilities:

items: Make decisions together on school strategy and operations
Monitor progress on SIP goals and KPIs
Review data and lead school improvement
Keep departments and programs consistent with each other
Model professional culture and leadership

content.text: These roles help the Principal deliver high-quality academic programs and student services:
content.title: School-Level Middle Leadership Roles

content.text:
Reports to: Primary or Secondary Principal (depending on level)

Collaborates with: Eduversal Subject Specialist (coordination, not a reporting line)

Scope: School Subject Leaders are appointed for core curriculum areas:
content.title: A. School Subject Leader (Koordinator Mata Pelajaran)

steps: Cambridge Core Subjects: English, Mathematics, Science (integrated), Physics, Chemistry, Biology
Indonesian National Subjects: Bahasa Indonesia, Pendidikan Pancasila dan Kewarganegaraan (PPKn), Religion (Islamic Studies / other faiths)
Cross-Curricular Programs: STEAM integration

content.text: Key Responsibilities:

steps: Lead implementation of the Cambridge curriculum in the assigned subject
Develop subject-specific schemes of work, assessments, and resources
Mentor and coach subject teachers; carry out peer observations
Work with Eduversal Subject Specialists on best practices
Support Olympiad preparation with subject expertise
Monitor student outcomes and recommend interventions
Make sure the curriculum is aligned with Cambridge standards and SLOs

content.text: Decision Rights:

steps: Recommend teaching resources and materials (within budget)
Design internal assessments and mark schemes
Organize subject-specific professional development
Give input on teacher recruitment and development plans

content.text:
Reports to: Primary / Secondary School Principal

Collaborates with: Eduversal Head of Olympiad Coordinators (EduOS)

Responsibilities:
content.title: B. School Olympiad Coordinator

steps: Identify and select students for academic competitions
Organize school-level olympiad training sessions
Coordinate participation in national and international competitions (mathematics, science, informatics)
Work with Subject Leaders on specialized coaching
Track student competition results and achievements
Build an Olympiad culture in the school

content.text: Decision Rights:

steps: Select students for competition participation
Schedule training sessions and mock competitions
Recommend external coaching resources (subject to GM approval)

content.text:
Reports to: Secondary Principal

Collaborates with: Eduversal Director of College Counseling

Responsibilities:

steps: Guide students through university applications (UCAS, Common App, local universities)
Help students develop personal statements and portfolios
Organize university fairs, campus visits, and alumni mentoring
Advise students on scholarships and financial aid
Keep track of university placements and report on them
Work with Subject Leaders on academic references
content.title: C. School College Counselor (Secondary Schools Only)

content.text: Decision Rights:

steps: Recommend university application strategies
Organize career guidance events (subject to budget)
Provide references and recommendation letters

content.text:
Reports to: Primary or Secondary Principal (depending on student age group)

Collaborates with: Eduversal Director of Extracurricular Coordination

Responsibilities:
content.title: D. School Extracurricular Coordinator

steps: Plan and oversee co-curricular activities: sports, arts, clubs, and community service
Make sure activities match the Profil Pelajar Pancasila and SLOs
Recruit and supervise activity coaches/instructors
Organize school events, competitions, and performances
Monitor student participation and engagement
Promote student leadership opportunities

content.text: Decision Rights:

steps: Design co-curricular program offerings (subject to GM approval)
Schedule activities and events
Recommend external instructors or partnerships

content.text: To keep Cambridge International School Centre status (see Section 3), schools must name:
content.title: Cambridge Centre-Specific Roles

steps: Usually: Secondary Principal
Responsibility: Overall accountability for Cambridge Centre compliance, exam integrity, and quality assurance
Authority: Makes the final decision on Cambridge exam policies at school level
content.title: A. Centre Head

steps: Reports to: Centre Head / Secondary Principal
Responsibility: Manage all Cambridge exam administration
Secure storage of exam materials
Candidate registration and entries
Invigilator training and exam conduct
Results processing and post-results services
Correspondence with Cambridge International
Authority: Day-to-day control of exam logistics and security
Attend HoD (Head of Department) meetings to align internal exams, Checkpoint and IGCSE preparation with academic plans.
Collect feedback from HoDs to improve exam quality and procedures.
Help teachers take part in Cambridge certificate programs, for professional growth and to align with international qualifications.
content.title: B. Exams Officer

steps: Reports to: Centre Head / General Manager
Responsibility:
Internal quality assurance and moderation
Main contact with Cambridge on standards and compliance
Monitors Centre standards (the Exams Officer prepares the Annual Centre Declaration and the Centre Head signs it)
Investigation of malpractice allegations
Authority: Recommend actions so the Centre complies with Cambridge standards
content.title: C. Quality Nominee

content.text:
Purpose: To identify, disclose and manage conflicts of interest that may harm honest decision-making.

Scope: Applies to Board members, Eduversal leadership, General Managers, Principals and SLT (Senior Leadership Team) members.

Definitions:

items: Conflict of Interest: A situation where personal, financial or professional interests may influence, or seem to influence, professional judgment or decisions.
Apparent Conflict: People believe there is a conflict, even if none exists.

content.text: Disclosure Requirements:

items: Annual Declaration: Everyone covered by this policy completes a Conflict of Interest Declaration Form at the start of each fiscal year (Appendix 1-A).
Ongoing Duty: Disclose a new conflict immediately when it arises (e.g., a family member applies for a job, or a business relationship with a vendor).

content.text: Examples of Conflicts:

items: Financial interest in a vendor or service provider to the school
A family member who works for, or is applying to work for, the network
A board or leadership position in a competing educational institution
Accepting gifts, hospitality or benefits from stakeholders above a small (nominal) value

content.text: Management Procedures:

steps: Disclosure: The person declares the conflict in writing to the Chair (Board) or the Chief Academic Officer (Staff).
Review: The Chair or CAO judges how significant (material) the conflict is and recommends how to manage it.

items: Recusal: The person stays out of the related discussions and decisions.
Divestment: Remove financial interest.
Monitoring: Increased transparency and oversight.
Prohibition: The activity or relationship must stop.

steps: Documentation: All conflicts, and the actions taken to manage them, are recorded in the Conflict of Interest Register.

Gifts and Hospitality Register: This covers all gifts, favors, meals or hospitality received in a professional role. Each one must be recorded in the Gifts and Hospitality Register (logbook or digital form). This prevents corruption, favoritism or the appearance of bias. Violations: Failure to disclose may lead to disciplinary action, including removal from the position.

content.text:
Purpose: To check how well the Board works, find areas to improve and build its governance capacity.

Process:

steps.text: Survey: Board members complete an anonymous self-evaluation survey (Appendix 1-B) covering:
items: Strategic oversight and direction
Financial stewardship
Policy development and compliance
Support for leadership
Board culture and dynamics
Individual contribution

steps: Analysis: The Chair and Secretary put the results together and identify themes.

Feedback from School Leadership: The Board also collects structured input from the General Manager and School Principals. The input covers how well the Board supports communication, decision-making and strategic direction. This improves transparency and alignment.
Reflection Session: The Board uses one meeting to discuss the findings and develop an improvement plan.
Action Plan: The Board commits to 2-3 priority improvement actions for the year (e.g., more financial literacy training, clearer role boundaries, stronger stakeholder engagement).
Progress Review: A mid-year check on progress with the action plan.

content.text: External Review: Every 3-5 years, the Board may arrange an independent governance review to add to its self-evaluation.
Purpose: To make sure oversight is systematic, compliance is maintained and strategic focus is kept throughout the year.
To meet CIS Domain E (Wellbeing; see the mapping in 18.2), the "Guidance Counseling" role must cover more than academic placement.

items: University & Career Counselor: Focuses on Cambridge destinations (UCAS/Common App) and career pathways.
Social-Emotional Counselor: A mandatory requirement for CIS/WASC to support student mental health and restorative practices.

Placement: This department reports structurally to the General Manager / Foundation Representative (through the Guidance Coordinator). It works closely with the Principal. It is not under the Principal's managerial supervision or evaluation.

content.text:
To show good governance and support accreditation, the following documents and records must be kept:

Board-Level Evidence:

items: Board Terms of Reference (Bylaws) and the 20-year Partnership MOUs (or interim Service Level Agreements for schools in transition)
Board meeting agendas, minutes, and resolutions (past 3 years)
Annual governance calendar
Board self-evaluation surveys and action plans
Annual Conflict of Interest Register and the Gifts and Hospitality Log
Strategic Plan (5-year) with annual updates
Combined network budget and financial reports
Chief Academic Officer performance evaluation
Board Self-Evaluation survey results and the Governance Improvement Action Plans that follow them

content.text: School-Level Evidence:

items: Partnership MOUs (20-year agreements with local Yayasan)
Organizational charts (network and school-specific)
General Manager job description and performance contract
School Improvement Plans (SIPs) with KPI dashboards
Twice-yearly reports to Eduversal and local Yayasan
Stakeholder meeting minutes (GM-Yayasan coordination)
Decision logs showing how the decision matrix is used
Valid National School Identification Number (NPSN) documentation and current school operational licenses
Teacher registration records in SIMPKB showing active NUPTK status for certified educators.
CIS/WASC Evidence: The "Standards Crosswalk", which links school activities to accreditation domains.
Student Wellbeing: Records of socio-emotional counseling sessions and university placement data.
Exam Integrity: Cambridge secure storage audit logs, invigilator training certificates, and incident logs.

content.title: International Baccalaureate (IB) — how it sits alongside this manual
items: No school in the Eduversal network runs an International Baccalaureate (IB) program. Some schools have said they are interested in becoming IB schools. So the framework is summarized here for reference. Nothing in this block describes a current obligation. These Academic Standards are built around the Cambridge pathway and Indonesian national requirements. They remain the standards that apply to every school in the network.

The governing IB document is Programme Standards and Practices (published October 2018, updated April 2020). It is organized in four pillars: Purpose (01), Environment (02), Culture (03) and Learning (04).

Its nine standards are: Purpose (0101); Leadership and governance (0201); Student support (0202); Teacher support (0203); Culture through policy implementation (0301); Designing a coherent curriculum (0401); Students as lifelong learners (0402); Approaches to teaching (0403); Approaches to assessment (0404). Individual practices carry codes of the form 0101-01-0100.

If a school is ever authorized to deliver an IB program, this precedence rule would apply. IB requirements govern that program on delivery, assessment and authorization. This manual continues to govern everything outside it. Indonesian law governs both. The rule is recorded now so the question does not have to be reopened later.

This manual deliberately has no separate IB section, and this is not a gap. A section written for zero schools would go out of date before anyone used it. The trigger for writing one is a school entering IB candidacy. At that point, the school works directly with the IB, using IB Programme Standards and Practices. This manual is then extended to cover the overlap. A school considering that step should raise it with Eduversal before applying. IB authorization brings curriculum, staffing and timetable commitments. These interact with the Cambridge pathway set out in Sections 5 and 6.
Source: IB Programme standards and practices (2020).
